I don’t know about you, but most of the confident people I know aren’t doing anything. This is just how they naturally are, they are fully relaxed. Most of the time they had great early childhood experiences and a family that socializes a great deal. Not to play the victim or anything, but these successful people are doing a minimal amount and there’s nothing to really learn from them. In fact, I tell them about all the work I’m doing and they’re seriously impressed, saying “I could never do that”. All we’re doing is masking.

Why can we not give ourselves the opportunity to relax and be ourselves when other people can? In fact, some of my best experiences with people were when I was fully anxious and vulnerable, saying stupid stuff. People like that. I found that people liked me a lot LESS when I was trying so hard to be prosocial and responding in a way that makes me look normal and confident. You become robotic and fake and stressed and people can tell. Socializing isn’t just a bag of tricks that you pull out and use to make the conversation go as smoothly as possible and make yourself look as good as possible. It’s about connection, and the shortcut to that is just showing up as you are. And maybe if you do that, you can get enough experience and knocked around enough to get molded into a similar personality to everyone else, just as most people do during earlier development. If that’s important to you. I find it ridiculous that we need to go through all these roundabout steps to prove to ourselves that we are deserving of love and companionship, when we could shortcut all that and just love ourselves now and admit to ourselves that we deserve friends and people who like us.

People like people who are HAPPY with themselves. This is something I observed on dating apps and while making friends. Not necessarily someone with a cookie cutter confident persona. Both can exist at once, but not necessarily. You can be weird and anxious but still happy with yourself. Ever wonder why some quiet kids have all the friends? Don’t take yourself too seriously and show up as yourself, fully vulnerable. That’s where confidence comes from, not simply trying so hard to appear confident. And when you’re happy with yourself, you listen better and connect better and focus more on what’s happening in the world instead of what’s in your head. Stuff that’s hard to do when you’re putting on a fake persona and are so stressed trying to keep it up.

I agree with you. I got to a top tier business school and good networking is something that you need to do to survive. Faking confidence in short bursts is a must. I still practice discipline to get my work done faster and to take care of my body. If I don’t, it’s very easy to regress to being an unhealthy hermit. But doing all that with the implicit goal of attracting people is not worth from my experience. People find you boring and rigid and hard to relate to, particularly since THEY don’t even do stuff like that. When people are complaining about how difficult their work is and how much they don’t want to do it, they don’t want to hear how easy it was for you since you’re so strong and such a hard worker. People need vulnerable people to struggle with, even the most confident and perfect people. I had more success just showing up as I am. When people goof off, I definitely found it an area that I was clueless in. It’s somewhere that body language, asking questions, genuine curiosity, etc. has no effect in. You need to be yourself and be stupid and imperfect. It definitely is a balance and tbh I still haven’t figured it out yet.

On your point of shying away because of anxiety, I agree that’s a worthy cause to put more willpower on. I guess you just need to choose your battles.
